monthly_review.summary: You've shifted dramatically toward higher-intensity running this month, with a sharp increase in Zone 4 and 5 effort — but at the cost of aerobic volume and efficiency. Pace improved significantly, yet average HR rose by 17 bpm and aerobic TE increased only modestly despite higher stress.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 4 effort jumped from 15% to 45% of total time while Zone 1+2 dropped from 53% to 10% — indicating a near-total absence of easy aerobic running this month.

goal_tracker.message: You need 44.5 more km across 9 additional sessions in the remaining 26 days — averaging ~4.9 km per session — to match last month's volume. Prioritize consistency over intensity: even 3–4 easy runs/week would close this gap meaningfully.

insights.title: Efficiency declined despite faster pace
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency dropped from 13.46 to 12.54 m/sec per bpm — meaning you're using more heart rate to sustain each unit of speed, likely due to reduced time in Z1–Z2 where capillary and mitochondrial adaptations occur.

insights.title: Near elimination of foundational aerobic work
insights.body: Z1+Z2 effort fell from 53% of total time last month to just 10% this month — well below the 70–80% recommended for sustainable aerobic base development in recreational runners.

insights.title: Improved stride length & reduced ground contact under higher intensity
insights.body: Stride length increased from 68.77 cm (June 21) to 75.73 cm (July 5), and ground contact time dropped from 314 ms to 305 ms — suggesting neuromuscular adaptation to faster efforts, but without corresponding aerobic support.

insights.title: High-intensity density without recovery buffer
insights.body: Your two July runs averaged 4.0 aerobic TE (vs 2.7 last month), yet VO2 max remains stable at 39.0 — signaling diminishing returns without lower-intensity volume to absorb and adapt to that stimulus.

recommendations.action: Do a 5 km Zone 2 run tomorrow at avg HR ≤135 bpm (based on your June 25 run HR of 135 at 9:34 min/km), focusing on relaxed breathing and cadence ≥152 spm.
recommendations.reason: To rebuild Z2 volume and improve aerobic efficiency — your lowest recent Z2 HR was 135, and Z2 should feel conversational to restore metabolic resilience.

recommendations.action: Add one 30-minute Zone 1 walk or very easy jog (HR ≤125 bpm) before your next hard session, using your Garmin's 'Recovery Time' metric as a guide — aim for <12 hrs recovery time before the next run.
recommendations.reason: Your recent high-Z4/Z5 runs (e.g., July 5 at 166 bpm, 4.0 TE) require adequate recovery; Zone 1 activity supports parasympathetic restoration without adding load.

recommendations.action: Perform a 6 km run at 9:00–9:15 min/km (540–555 sec/km), targeting avg HR 138–142 bpm and cadence ≥152 spm — matching your June 28 effort but extending duration to reinforce aerobic pacing.
recommendations.reason: This bridges your current Z3-heavy pattern (23% this month) back toward sustainable Z2–Z3 balance, improving fatigue resistance at goal pace.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish neural and metabolic familiarity with low-heart-rate, high-efficiency running — prioritizing time-in-zone over pace, rebuilding capillary density, and restoring HR-pacing intuition.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 Foundation Run (5 km, HR ≤135 bpm)
Zone 1 Active Recovery (30 min walk or jog, HR ≤125 bpm)
Z2–Z3 Bridge Run (6 km, HR 138–142 bpm, 9:00–9:15 min/km)
